command:
mkdir -p /data/db/tls && if [ ! -s /data/db/tls/mongodb.pem ]; then printf '[req]
distinguished_name=dn
prompt=no
x509_extensions=v3
[dn]
C=JP
ST=Tokyo
L=Chiyoda
O=NII
OU=GRDM dev
CN=mongo
[v3]
subjectAltName=DNS:mongo
basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE
' > /tmp/mongo-cert.cnf && openssl req -newkey rsa:2048 -new -x509 -days 9999 -nodes -config /tmp/mongo-cert.cnf -out /data/db/tls/mongodb.crt -keyout /data/db/tls/mongodb.key && cat /data/db/tls/mongodb.key /data/db/tls/mongodb.crt > /data/db/tls/mongodb.pem && rm -f /data/db/tls/mongodb.key; fi && cp /data/db/tls/mongodb.crt /mongo-tls/mongodb.crt && chmod 0644 /mongo-tls/mongodb.crt && chown -R mongodb:mongodb /data/db && chmod 0600 /data/db/tls/mongodb.pem && exec gosu mongodb mongod --sslMode requireSSL --sslDisabledProtocols=TLS1_0,TLS1_1 --sslPEMKeyFile /data/db/tls/mongodb.pem
note: The server key stays in mongo_data; only the public certificate is copied to mongo_tls, which sharejs mounts read-only as its trust anchor (ADR-07). The certificate is made once and survives restarts, so a client that trusted it keeps working.
